Image: Planet Labs Advertisement For years, Khasan was little more than a very remote place on the edge of Russia . Less than 500 people live in the village in the country's far east, more than 5,600 miles (9,012 kilometers) from Moscow. But it's here that Russia shares a mere 10.5-mile border with North Korea — and Khasan is the only Russian settlement along that short stretch. Since 1959, the so-called Korean-Russian Friendship Railway Bridge has crossed the Tumen River here, serving as the only land connection between the two countries. stories.article_text_excerpt: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Officials say two people were killed in the attack on Gaza City By Jamie Whitehead Published 2 August 2026, 15:46 BST Updated 3 hours ago At least 13 people, including several children, have been killed in the latest strikes on Gaza, Palestinian officials have said. Gaza's Civil Defence Authority said Israeli military aircraft carried out the attacks on Gaza City, Khan Younis and Deir el-Balah. It was the second successive night of Israeli strikes on the territory, and it comes days after Hamas accepted a disarmament plan, which would see the Palestinian group hand over its weapons to US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace. However, another 16 years would pass before marriage itself became an option. "The Civil Partnership Act was a milestone for the legal recognition of same-sex couples in Germany and laid the foundation for opening up marriage," Alexander Vogt of the national board of " Queere Vielfalt e.V. " (Queer diversity) told DW. "It introduced a legally secure partnership with rights similar to those of marriage — such as inheritance, maintenance, and residency rights — though it remained discriminatory in many areas – like adoption or tax law. Nevertheless, it gave us a foot in the door — a solid base from which further rights could be secured, usually by appealing to the Federal Constitutional Court ." stories.title: Spain will send troops to Ceuta to help with border security
stories.summary: Authorities in the Spanish city of Ceuta asked Madrid to declare a national emergency and send military assistance. Crowds of people breached the border of the territory next to Morocco as police lost control.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5I1Ze Video footage showed large crowds moving round the breakwater Image: Atlas/REUTERS Advertisement Officials in the Spanish territory of Ceuta on the northwestern tip of Africa on Thursday asked the government in Madrid to declare a national emergency and send the army to help secure its border with Morocco . The call came as video footage showed crowds of people trying to walk around the breakwaters separating Moroccan and Spanish territory or otherwise scale the border fence. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez pledged an "immediate response." Spain's Interior Ministry said later on Thursday that its armed forces would send personnel to Ceuta to support the border guards. "The Armed Forces will reinforce the Guardia Civil in the exercise of its powers and any others that may be necessary to maintain civil security in the city of Ceuta," the ministry said. What had happened in Ceuta during the day? The Guardia Civil said that crowds broke through the fences into Spain after overwhelming police at the city's breakwater. stories.title: Spain's PM visits Ceuta after thousands breached border
stories.summary: Thousands of people continued pouring into Ceuta from Morocco during the night, after Spanish police lost control of the border. The head of the city government estimated that 60,000 people had entered.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5I40g Spanish authorities were overwhelmed by the latest influx Image: Atlas/REUTERS Advertisement Editors note: For more on the migrant crisis in Ceuta, Spain, follow our blog here . Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez , his interior minister and military personnel were bound for the North African enclave of Ceuta on Friday, a day after thousands of people gained irregular entry to the Spanish territory . At least 18 people died as tens of thousands of people rushed into the small Spanish coastal city, many of them drowning but some also perishing in a stampede to cross the breakwater fence. Authorities are still puzzling over what prompted such large crowds to suddenly seek entry. Regional government head estimates 60,000 new arrivals Preliminary estimates suggest that tens of thousands gained entry on Thursday alone as the Guardia Civil lost control of the border to Morocco . The head of the autonomous city governemnt, Juan Jesus Vivas, estimated that around 60,000 people had arrived, well over half Ceuta's population.
